message.content:
Repo: C:\Users\jotac\OneDrive\Documents\DEV\serer_delivery (NestJS/TypeScript backend) and C:\Users\jotac\OneDrive\Documents\DEV\deliveryhub_white_label (React/Vite frontend, "DeliveryHub" delivery platform).

I need to understand how CUSTOMER and RESTAURANT OWNER accounts currently use real Supabase Auth (login, registration, password reset/"forgot password"), because I'm about to migrate a separate custom-JWT motoboy (courier) auth system to also use real Supabase Auth, following the same pattern.

Please investigate and report:

1. Backend: How is a customer/restaurant-owner Supabase Auth user created? Look at `src/onboarding/onboarding.controller.ts` (`registrarInicial`) and any customer registration service — does it call `supabase.auth.admin.createUser()` or use the client-side `supabase.auth.signUp()`? What does `user_profiles` table look like as the profile companion table (columns, how it links to `auth.users.id`)?

2. Backend: is there ANY password-reset/forgot-password endpoint already implemented for customers/owners (e.g. wrapping `supabase.auth.resetPasswordForEmail` or `supabase.auth.admin.generateLink`)? Search broadly (`resetPassword`, `forgotPassword`, `recuperar-senha`, `esqueci-senha`, `reset-password`). Report exact file/route if found, or confirm it's entirely handled client-side via the Supabase JS SDK directly (no backend involvement needed).

3. Backend: how do NestJS guards authenticate customer/owner requests using Supabase Auth tokens? (e.g. `SupabaseAuthGuard`, `RestaurantOwnerGuard`) — how do they verify the `Authorization` header, and how does `req.userId`/`req.userRole` get populated? Reference `src/auth/` directory.

4. Frontend: find the `AuthContext` (or equivalent) in `deliveryhub_white_label/src/` — how does customer/owner login work (`supabase.auth.signInWithPassword`?), how is the session persisted (localStorage key, `onAuthStateChange`?), and is there a "forgot password" UI/flow already built (look for pages/components with "esqueci"/"recuperar"/"reset" in the name, and any `supabase.auth.resetPasswordForEmail` call)?

5. Frontend: how does `isMotoboy()` in AuthContext currently work, and how does the customer/owner login page (`customer-registration-login` or similar) differ from where a motoboy would need to log in? Is there a single unified login page today or separate ones per role?

Report file:line references and concise code snippets for each of these 5 points. Don't propose solutions — just report what exists today so we can design the motoboy migration to match this existing pattern.

Now I have a complete picture. Here's the full report.

## 1. Backend: how is a customer/restaurant-owner Supabase Auth user created?

**No backend endpoint creates customer/owner Supabase Auth users at all.** `src/restaurante/onboarding.controller.ts` (`registrarInicial`, line 95-189) never touches `supabase.auth.admin.*`. It's `@UseGuards(JwtGuard)` — it assumes `req.userId` already exists (i.e., the Supabase Auth user was already created client-side before hitting this endpoint) and only creates a `restaurants` row keyed on that `user_id`.

Account creation happens entirely client-side via `supabase.auth.signUp()` — see point 4 below. There is no backend "register customer" service/controller in `serer_delivery` at all (searched broadly for `auth.admin.createUser`, `auth.signUp` in `src/` — zero matches).

The **only** place the backend creates/mutates a Supabase Auth user is admin-initiated, in `src/usuarios/usuarios.service.ts:97-143` (`trocarCredenciais`), which calls `supabase.auth.admin.updateUserById()` — support tooling for admins to force-reset another user's email/password, not self-registration.

**`user_profiles` table** (companion profile row, PK = `auth.users.id`, presumably auto-created by a DB trigger on `auth.users` insert — no such trigger file exists in this repo, so it must live in the Supabase project itself):
- Columns observed across queries: `id` (uuid, = `auth.users.id`), `name`, `email`, `role` (`customer` | `restaurant_owner` | `motoboy` | `admin`), `must_change_password`, `created_at`, `updated_at`.
- Role starts as `'customer'` (set via `signUp` metadata, see point 4) and gets elevated server-side later: `UsuariosService.elevarSeNecessario`/`rebaixarSeOrfao` (`src/usuarios/usuarios.service.ts:33-68`) flips it to `restaurant_owner` when a `restaurants.user_id` is linked, and `MotoboyAuthService.vincularContaCliente` (`src/motoboy/motoboy-auth.service.ts:65-77`) flips it to `motoboy`.
- A separate `customers` table (not `user_profiles`) holds the actual customer profile data, keyed by `customers.user_id -> auth.users.id`, columns: `id, name, email, phone_e164, address_json, foto_perfil_url, lat, lng, address_geocode_hash, address_geocoded_at` (`src/perfil/perfil.service.ts:5,36-57`). It's lazily created on first `getMeuPerfil` call from `user_profiles.name/email`.

## 2. Backend: any password-reset/forgot-password endpoint?

**None exists on the backend.** Grepped `src/` for `resetPassword|forgotPassword|recuperar-senha|esqueci-senha|reset-password|forgot-password` (case-insensitive) — zero matches. It's handled entirely client-side via the Supabase JS SDK directly:

- `deliveryhub_white_label/src/services/authService.js:114-125` — `resetPassword(email)` calls `supabase.auth.resetPasswordForEmail(email, { redirectTo: `${origin}/reset-password` })`.
- `authService.js:89-97` — `updatePassword(newPassword)` calls `supabase.auth.updateUser({ password: newPassword })` (used once already logged in, e.g. after clicking the reset link).

**Notable gap**: `redirectTo` points to `/reset-password`, but that route is **not registered** in `deliveryhub_white_label/src/Routes.jsx` (full route list checked, no `/reset-password` entry — it would 404 into the catch-all `<Route path="*" element={<NotFound />} />` at line 159). So the "forgot password" email-link flow is wired on the send side but the landing page to actually set a new password doesn't exist yet in this frontend.

## 3. Backend: how do guards authenticate customer/owner requests?

`src/auth/supabase-jwt.service.ts` (`SupabaseJwtService.verificar`, lines 23-33) verifies the raw Supabase Auth JWT using **JWKS** (not the Supabase client SDK's own verify): decodes the token, fetches the signing key from `${SUPABASE_URL}/auth/v1/.well-known/jwks.json` via `jwks-rsa`, and does `jwt.verify()` with that public key.

`src/auth/jwt.guard.ts` (`JwtGuard.canActivate`, lines 13-26): pulls `Authorization: Bearer <token>` header, calls `supabaseJwt.verificar(token)`, and on success sets:
```ts
request.userId = verified.sub;
request.userRole = verified.user_metadata?.role ?? 'customer';
```
Throws `UnauthorizedException` if missing/invalid.

`src/auth/restaurant-owner.guard.ts` (`RestaurantOwnerGuard`, lines 8-58): composes on top — calls `jwtGuard.canActivate(context)` first, then looks up `restaurants` by `user_id = request.userId`; if none found, throws `ForbiddenException`. It also enforces White-Label custom-domain ownership (Origin/Referer check) and sets `request.restaurantId`.

`src/auth/admin.guard.ts` (`AdminGuard`, lines 12-29): same composition pattern — runs `jwtGuard.canActivate`, then checks `user_profiles.role === 'admin'`.

Note the role check for admin/owner guards reads the **live** `user_profiles.role`/`restaurants` table (DB-authoritative), not just the JWT's embedded `user_metadata.role`, which is only used as the `JwtGuard`'s own default (`request.userRole`).

## 4. Frontend: AuthContext — login, session persistence, forgot-password UI

`deliveryhub_white_label/src/contexts/AuthContext.jsx`:
- `signIn(email, password)` (lines 83-111) → `supabase.auth.signInWithPassword({ email, password })`.
- `signUp(email, password, userData)` (lines 113-148) → `supabase.auth.signUp({ email, password, options: { data: { name, role: userData.role || 'customer', ...userData } } })` — role is passed as **Supabase Auth `user_metadata`** at signup time; presumably a DB trigger on `auth.users` copies this into `user_profiles.role` (trigger not present in repo, must be Supabase-side SQL).
- Session bootstrap: `useEffect` (lines 22-51) calls `supabase.auth.getSession()` once on mount, then subscribes via `supabase.auth.onAuthStateChange((event, session) => ...)` to keep `user`/`userProfile` state in sync (comment explicitly warns "NEVER ASYNC callback").
- `fetchUserProfile(userId)` (lines 73-81) does `supabase.from('user_profiles').select('*').eq('id', userId).single()` after every session change.
- Session persistence itself is delegated to the Supabase JS client config in `src/lib/supabase.js:23-28`: `createClient(url, anonKey, { auth: { autoRefreshToken: true, persistSession: true } })` — no custom `storageKey` override, so it uses the SDK default localStorage key `sb-<project-ref>-auth-token`.
- `signOut()` (lines 150-165) calls `supabase.auth.signOut()`.

**Forgot-password UI**: `deliveryhub_white_label/src/pages/customer-registration-login/components/ForgotPasswordModal.jsx` — a modal (email input → "Enviar Link de Recuperação") triggered from the login page. It's purely presentational; the actual call happens in the parent page: `customer-registration-login/index.jsx:86-88`:
```js
const handleForgotPassword = async (email) => {
  await authService.resetPassword(email);
};
```
which calls into `authService.resetPassword` → `supabase.auth.resetPasswordForEmail` (point 2 above). As noted, the post-click landing page (`/reset-password`) that would call `authService.updatePassword` doesn't exist in `Routes.jsx`.

Also relevant: `src/pages/admin-trocar-senha/index.jsx` and `src/components/perfil/CredenciaisForm.jsx` are separate self-service "change email/password while logged in" flows (using `authService.updateEmail`/`updatePassword`), distinct from the forgot-password flow.

## 5. Frontend: `isMotoboy()` and login page structure

`isMotoboy()` (`AuthContext.jsx:184-186`):
```js
const isMotoboy = () => userProfile?.role === 'motoboy';
```
Just reads the Supabase-derived `user_profiles.role` — pure client-side Supabase Auth flag. (Backend's `PerfilService.ehMotoboy`, `src/perfil/perfil.service.ts:18-32`, notes this doesn't catch the case where a motoboy record exists in the separate `motoboys` table with the same email but no `user_id` link — a legacy-account edge case.)

**There is a single unified login page today**, `customer-registration-login/index.jsx`, that handles customer AND restaurant-owner login (and registration) through Supabase Auth. Crucially, it also has a **fallback to the legacy motoboy custom-JWT system** baked in (`handleLogin`, lines 37-66): if `signIn` (Supabase) fails, it silently retries via `motoboyLogin(formData.emailOrPhone, formData.password)` (`src/services/motoboyAuthService.js`, hitting `POST /api/motoboy/auth/login` on the backend, custom `MOTOBOY_JWT_SECRET`-signed JWT, stored under `localStorage['motoboy_access_token']`), and on success redirects to `/motoboy` and stores the token via `setMotoboyToken`.

Motoboys otherwise have **their own separate routes** distinct from the unified customer/owner page:
- `/motoboy` and `/motoboy/login` → `MotoboyPortal` (guarded by `src/components/MotoboyGuard.jsx`, which just checks `localStorage.getItem('motoboy_access_token')` / `?token=` URL param — no Supabase involvement at all today).
- `/motoboy/cadastro` → `MotoboyCadastro` (separate registration form, posts to `POST /api/motoboy/auth/cadastro`, backend `MotoboyAuthService.cadastro`, `src/motoboy/motoboy-auth.service.ts:135-180`, which bcrypt-hashes a password into `motoboys.password_hash` — no Supabase Auth user created there today, only an optional cross-link if `supabase_access_token` is passed for an already-logged-in customer session).

The owner/customer `RestauranteGuard` (`src/components/RestauranteGuard.jsx`), by contrast, is fully Supabase-driven: reads `isAuthenticated()`/`isRestaurantOwner()` from `AuthContext`, redirecting unauthenticated users to `/customer-registration-login` (the unified page) with `state={{ from: location.pathname }}` for post-login redirect.
